text:
Priya (Eng Manager): Hey team — new hire starts Mon. Can someone drop a concise manager onboarding checklist? Need day-by-day agenda + a 30/60/90 sketch and who to loop in for access/equipment.
Taylor (People Ops): @Priya — putting a compact "Manager Launchpad" here you can copy. I’ll also add to the shared folder and create calendar invites.
Taylor (People Ops): Day -1 (prestart): create SSO account, add to Slack + relevant channels, assign buddy, confirm laptop shipping, send welcome email with first-week agenda.
Taylor (People Ops): Day 1: Team intros (30m), 1:1 with manager (45m), systems access walkthrough (30m), quick pairing on a tiny onboarding task (30m).
Taylor (People Ops): Day 2: Product & infra demo (60m), review docs for runtime basics, checklist for dev environment + submit any additional access requests to IT.
Taylor (People Ops): Day 3: Shadowing + doc walkthrough, 30m meeting to outline 30/60/90 goals with manager, assign initial small-owner task.
Taylor (People Ops): Day 4: Meet with cross-functional partners (pm/devops/security), hands-on pairing, soft-landing project scoping.
Taylor (People Ops): Day 5: Recap 1:1, feedback, finalize 30/60/90 draft and share with skip-level.
Taylor (People Ops): 30/60/90 quick template (one-liners you can adapt):
- 30d: Learn the stack + contribute small PRs; complete core docs & security training.
- 60d: Own a small feature or infra task end-to-end; reduce an onboarding friction.
- 90d: Deliver first measurable outcome (user-facing or infra cost/latency win) and propose two improvements.
Taylor (People Ops): Manager tips: block focused time for the new hire, set daily async check-ins first week, give a clear "first small win" task, and share team working norms.
Taylor (People Ops): Copyable calendar invite examples:
```
Invite: "Welcome + Team intro"
When: Mon 10:00-11:00
Attendees: newhire, manager, team leads, buddy
Agenda: intros / expectations / first-week plan
```
```
Invite: "Dev setup & env pairing"
When: Tue 14:00-15:00
Attendees: newhire, mentor, infra eng
Agenda: dev box imaging, SSH/git, run tests
```
Aisha (HR): I’ll assemble the offer packet, benefits links, and payroll setup instructions. Also: new hire must complete Security & Privacy training by day 7.
Mark (IT): Laptop order placed and imaging scheduled for Fri. Need shipping address + whether mac/linux preference. Also please open a ticket for repo/Jira/GCP access with the exact team names.
Priya (Eng Manager): Sending address now. Can Sam be the buddy?
Sam (Mentor): happy to be buddy. I can do a quick "first-week dev setup" drop-in Wed 3pm and stay available for quick pairing.
onboard-bot: Created folder and added checklist: https://redwood.internal/onboarding/manager-launchpad — also attached a template 30-60-90 doc.
Priya (Eng Manager): Any recommended reading specific to the inference/runtime teams for the first week?
Taylor (People Ops): send them the Learning Path: https://redwood.internal/learning/inference-runtime and flag "Serving runtime basics" + "Observability & cost controls". That covers the first-week context.
Aisha (HR): reminder: complete I-9 and benefits enrollment tasks before payroll cutoff (link in the packet).
Mark (IT): if you need SSH keys earlier, file a ticket now and we'll expedite.
Priya (Eng Manager): Great — I’ll post a short welcome blurb in #general on Monday morning and share the calendar invites. :tada:
Taylor (People Ops): Sample welcome blurb you can copy: "Please welcome Alex Chen, joining as Staff Software Engineer on the Inference team. Alex will be focusing on latency and cost optimization. Say hi and share any tips for day 1!" We’ll also send the org chart and team expectations doc.
Priya (Eng Manager): Perfect — thanks everyone. This is super actionable.
